prediction:
THOUGHT: The clinical picture is of long-standing, progressive indurated erythematous plaques with scarring and contracture, without systemic symptoms. Microscopy (KOH) showed budding yeasts and arthrospores; biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with hyaline hyphae, spores and budding yeasts that were PAS- and silver-positive. Culture grew a Trichosporon species and PCR/DNA sequencing identified Trichosporon mycotoxinivorans. Those microbiologic and histopathologic findings are diagnostic and explain the chronic cutaneous granulomatous lesions. Differential considerations include other deep fungal infections and chronic granulomatous cutaneous diseases that can produce long-standing plaques and scarring.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Chronic cutaneous trichosporonosis (cutaneous infection due to Trichosporon mycotoxinivorans) — confirmed by culture and PCR with supportive KOH and histology.
2. Phaeohyphomycosis (deep cutaneous infection by dematiaceous fungi) — clinically and histologically can mimic chronic granulomatous plaques with hyphal elements.
3. Chromoblastomycosis — chronic verrucous/plaque-forming fungal infection producing granulomas and scarring (would show sclerotic/muriform bodies on histology, not seen here).
4. Sporotrichosis (cutaneous/lymphocutaneous Sporothrix schenckii complex infection) — chronic subcutaneous nodules/plaques with granulomas; often a clinical mimic.
5. Lupus vulgaris (cutaneous tuberculosis) — chronic indurated plaque with scarring and contracture as a nonfungal granulomatous mimic (less likely given negative Mantoux and fungal confirmation).
ground_truth: Primary cutaneous trichosporonosis caused by Trichosporon mycotoxinivorans

Case Information:
A woman in her 20s presented with a large erythematous indurated plaque involving the face and neck that had been first noted at age 2 years. The plaque progressively increased in size, and similar plaques developed over the back, right dorsal surface of the hand, suprapubic area, and right thigh over the last 4 years. Scarring developed in the plaques over the face and hand during the course of the disease and led to flexion contracture of the hand with limitation of movement. There were no constitutional symptoms. There was no history of trauma preceding these lesions. She had received multiple previous treatments without significant improvement.

Physical Examination:
Well-defined erythematous plaque of 7 × 8 cm over the suprapubic area. Additional plaques present on face, neck, back, right dorsal surface of hand, and right thigh. Flexion contracture of the hand with limited movement noted.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Laboratory Tests:
  * Routine hematological and biochemical investigations were normal
  * Mantoux test showed an induration of 2 × 1 mm at 48 hours

- Imaging Studies:
  * Chest radiography was normal

- Pathological Studies:
  * Direct potassium hydroxide preparation: Multiple budding yeast cells and arthrospores observed
  * Skin biopsy: Granulomatous infiltrate with giant cells, lymphocytes, histiocytes, neutrophils, and eosinophils. Hyaline hyphae branching at acute angles with multiple spores and budding yeasts, positive for silver methenamine and periodic acid–Schiff stains
  * Culture: Grew Trichosporon species, identified as Trichosporon mycotoxinivorans through PCR analysis and DNA sequencing

  * Figure 2A Title: Potassium hydroxide preparation showing fungal elements
  * Figure 2B Title: Periodic acid–Schiff staining showing inflammatory infiltrate and fungal elements
  * Figure 2C Title: Culture plate showing Trichosporon colonies
